claim: BLM is a multifunctional helicase that plays critical roles in maintaining genome stability.
source: BLM is a multifunctional helicase that plays critical roles in maintaining genome stability.
evidence: This is a general statement about BLM's role, supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: BLM processes distinct DNA substrates, but not nicked DNA, during many steps in DNA replication and repair.
source: It processes distinct DNA substrates, but not nicked DNA, during many steps in DNA replication and repair.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about BLM's substrate specificity.

claim: A high abundance of BLMs can unidirectionally unwind dsDNA from a nick when an external destabilizing force is applied.
source: using a combined single-molecule approach, we find that a high abundance of BLMs can indeed unidirectionally unwind dsDNA from a nick when an external destabilizing force is applied.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from single-molecule experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Human replication protein A (hRPA) ensures that limited quantities of BLMs processively unwind nicked dsDNA under a reduced force.
source: human replication protein A (hRPA) not only ensures that limited quantities of BLMs processively unwind nicked dsDNA under a reduced force
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: hRPA permits the translocation of BLMs on both intact and nicked ssDNAs, resulting in a bidirectional unwinding mode.
source: but also permits the translocation of BLMs on both intact and nicked ssDNAs, resulting in a bidirectional unwinding mode.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing bidirectional unwinding in the presence of RPA.

claim: BLM activation by RPA necessitates BLM targeting on the nick.
source: This activation necessitates BLM targeting on the nick and the presence of free hRPAs in solution whereas direct interactions between them are dispensable.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from sequential protein incubation assays.

claim: BLM activation by RPA requires the presence of free hRPAs in solution.
source: This activation necessitates BLM targeting on the nick and the presence of free hRPAs in solution whereas direct interactions between them are dispensable.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from channel-switching experiments.

claim: Direct interactions between BLM and RPA are dispensable for BLM activation.
source: This activation necessitates BLM targeting on the nick and the presence of free hRPAs in solution whereas direct interactions between them are dispensable.
evidence: This claim is supported by experiments with core-BLM lacking RPA-binding domains.

claim: RecQ family helicases have been highly conserved during evolution from prokaryotes to humans.
source: Among these DNA helicases, the RecQ family helicases have been highly conserved during evolution from prokaryotes to humans and play critical roles in genome maintenance and stability (Bernstein et al., 2010; Croteau et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: RecQ family helicases play critical roles in genome maintenance and stability.
source: Among these DNA helicases, the RecQ family helicases have been highly conserved during evolution from prokaryotes to humans and play critical roles in genome maintenance and stability (Bernstein et al., 2010; Croteau et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Defects in BLM, WRN and RECQ4 give rise to distinct heritable human disease syndromes.
source: Defects in three of the five human RecQ members (BLM, WRN and RECQ4) give rise to distinct heritable human disease syndromes (Bloom's, Werner's and Rothmund-Thomson syndromes, respectively), characterized by genomic instability and an increased incidence of cancers (Ellis et al., 1995; Kitao et al., 1999; Yu et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Bloom's, Werner's and Rothmund-Thomson syndromes are characterized by genomic instability and an increased incidence of cancers.
source: Defects in three of the five human RecQ members (BLM, WRN and RECQ4) give rise to distinct heritable human disease syndromes (Bloom's, Werner's and Rothmund-Thomson syndromes, respectively), characterized by genomic instability and an increased incidence of cancers (Ellis et al., 1995; Kitao et al., 1999; Yu et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BLM unwinds DNA in a 3'−5' direction.
source: Bloom syndrome protein (BLM) is one of the five RecQ family helicases that unwind DNA in a 3'−5' direction (Croteau et al., 2014; Karow et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BLM is involved in DNA end resection.
source: It is involved in many aspects of genome maintenance, including DNA end resection (Kowalczykowski, 2015), displacement-loop (D-loop) processing (Bugreev et al., 2007), rescuing stalled or collapsed replication forks (Davies et al., 2007), and resolution of Holliday junction (Bizard and Hickson, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BLM is involved in displacement-loop (D-loop) processing.
source: It is involved in many aspects of genome maintenance, including DNA end resection (Kowalczykowski, 2015), displacement-loop (D-loop) processing (Bugreev et al., 2007), rescuing stalled or collapsed replication forks (Davies et al., 2007), and resolution of Holliday junction (Bizard and Hickson, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BLM is involved in rescuing stalled or collapsed replication forks.
source: It is involved in many aspects of genome maintenance, including DNA end resection (Kowalczykowski, 2015), displacement-loop (D-loop) processing (Bugreev et al., 2007), rescuing stalled or collapsed replication forks (Davies et al., 2007), and resolution of Holliday junction (Bizard and Hickson, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BLM is involved in resolution of Holliday junction.
source: It is involved in many aspects of genome maintenance, including DNA end resection (Kowalczykowski, 2015), displacement-loop (D-loop) processing (Bugreev et al., 2007), rescuing stalled or collapsed replication forks (Davies et al., 2007), and resolution of Holliday junction (Bizard and Hickson, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BLM can unwind G-quadruplex structures.
source: BLM's diverse functions are realized by its remarkable unwinding capabilities of many unique DNA structures, such as G-quadruplex (Chatterjee et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BLM participates in many steps in repairing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) via homologous recombination (HR).
source: In particular, BLM has been verified to participate in many steps in repairing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) via homologous recombination (HR) (Nimonkar et al., 2011; Nimonkar et al., 2008; Sturzenegger et al., 2014; Woglar and Villeneuve, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BLM is recruited to DSB ends and facilitates resection of the 5' termini to generate 3' end protruding ssDNAs in the first step of HR.
source: It has been demonstrated to be recruited to the DSB ends and facilitate resection of the 5' termini to generate 3' end protruding ssDNAs in the first step of HR (Gravel et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BLM unwinds dsDNA to provide ssDNA for exonuclease resection by EXO1 or DNA2.
source: BLM either unwinds dsDNA to provide ssDNA for exonuclease resection by EXO1 or DNA2 or directly stimulates their nucleolytic activities (Nimonkar et al., 2008; Sturzenegger et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BLM directly stimulates the nucleolytic activities of EXO1 or DNA2.
source: BLM either unwinds dsDNA to provide ssDNA for exonuclease resection by EXO1 or DNA2 or directly stimulates their nucleolytic activities (Nimonkar et al., 2008; Sturzenegger et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BLM alone is unable to initiate dsDNA unwinding from a nick in vitro.
source: Paradoxically, even though BLM is distinctive in preferentially unwinding unique substrates (Mohaghegh et al., 2001), an in vitro ensemble study has demonstrated that this helicase alone is unable to initiate dsDNA unwinding from a nick which is a prevalent and essential DNA intermediate during HR (Maizels and Davis, 2018; Mohaghegh et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A nick is a prevalent and essential DNA intermediate during HR.
source: Paradoxically, even though BLM is distinctive in preferentially unwinding unique substrates (Mohaghegh et al., 2001), an in vitro ensemble study has demonstrated that this helicase alone is unable to initiate dsDNA unwinding from a nick which is a prevalent and essential DNA intermediate during HR (Maizels and Davis, 2018; Mohaghegh et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BLM's varying unwinding activities are often regulated by other in vivo factors.
source: These contradictory findings may be reconciled by BLM's varying unwinding activities, which are often regulated by other in vivo factors (Croteau et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BLM helicase interacts and collaborates with many protein partners to aid in cellular responses to replication stress and DNA damage in vivo.
source: It has been widely appreciated that the BLM helicase interacts and collaborates with many protein partners to aid in cellular responses to replication stress and DNA damage in vivo (Croteau et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Interactions and collaborations between BLM and protein partners dictate BLM's specialized functions in genome maintenance.
source: These interactions and collaborations dictate BLM's specialized functions in genome maintenance.
evidence: This is an inference based on the established knowledge about protein-protein interactions.

claim: RPA is a heterotrimeric protein complex consisting of the RPA70, RPA32 and RPA14 subunits.
source: A key partner of BLM is the single-stranded DNA-binding (SSB) protein, replication protein A (RPA), a heterotrimeric protein complex consisting of the RPA70, RPA32 and RPA14 subunits, which is also essential in DNA repair and recombination (Fanning et al., 2006; Wold, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: RPA is essential in DNA repair and recombination.
source: A key partner of BLM is the single-stranded DNA-binding (SSB) protein, replication protein A (RPA), a heterotrimeric protein complex consisting of the RPA70, RPA32 and RPA14 subunits, which is also essential in DNA repair and recombination (Fanning et al., 2006; Wold, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: RPA co-localizes with BLM at the foci of DNA damage.
source: A recent in vivo study directly demonstrated that RPA co-localizes with BLM at the foci of DNA damage, suggesting that these two proteins coordinate and function together in DNA repair (Woglar and Villeneuve, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: RPA physically interacts with BLM.
source: In addition, biochemical, structural and single-molecule studies have revealed that RPA not only physically interacts with BLM but also stimulates its unwinding activity by increasing its processivity or improving its unwinding initiation (Brosh et al., 2000; Doherty et al., 2005; Soniat et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: RPA stimulates BLM's unwinding activity by increasing its processivity or improving its unwinding initiation.
source: In addition, biochemical, structural and single-molecule studies have revealed that RPA not only physically interacts with BLM but also stimulates its unwinding activity by increasing its processivity or improving its unwinding initiation (Brosh et al., 2000; Doherty et al., 2005; Soniat et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The poor ability of a heterologous SSB protein to stimulate BLM's unwinding suggests that this stimulation is specific.
source: The poor ability of a heterologous SSB protein to stimulate BLM's unwinding further suggests that this stimulation is specific (Brosh et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In the presence of 20 nM BLM, apparent dsDNA unwinding was not observed over a broad force range from 10 pN to 40 pN.
source: In the presence of 20 nM BLM, apparent dsDNA unwinding was not observed over a broad force range from 10 pN to 40 pN (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: At a high BLM concentration of 200 nM, one or few unwinding events on a single DNA molecule were recorded once the force was increased to a range of 10–40 pN in all examined traces (n = 30).
source: In contrast, at a high BLM concentration of 200 nM, one or few unwinding events on a single DNA molecule were recorded once the force was increased to a range of 10–40 pN in all examined traces (n = 30) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with sample size n=30.

claim: Omitting ATP did not result in changes in either fluorescence or DNA length signal, confirming that observations were a result of BLM-catalyzed dsDNA unwinding.
source: Omitting ATP did not result in changes in either fluorescence or DNA length signal in this experimental condition, confirming that our observations were a result of BLM-catalyzed dsDNA unwinding (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a control experiment confirming ATP-dependence of the observed activity.

claim: Control experiments without Sytox exhibited similar DNA length increases in the presence of BLM, suggesting that the fluorescent dye does not affect BLM's unwinding activities.
source: Control experiments without Sytox exhibited similar DNA length increases in the presence of BLM, suggesting that the fluorescent dye does not affect BLM's unwinding activities (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a control experiment showing that Sytox does not interfere with BLM activity.

claim: In all 49 examined events from 33 traces, the unwinding progressed in one direction only.
source: In all 49 examined events from 33 traces, the unwinding progressed in one direction only, as reflected by the progression of the dark region of the fluorescence signal as well as the biased disappearance of its adjacent dsDNA (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 49 events across 33 traces.

claim: The observed dsDNA unwinding was initiated from a nick rather than by melting dsDNA internally.
source: This finding is not consistent with the possibility that the observed dsDNA unwinding was initiated by melting dsDNA internally where bidirectional progression of the unwinding fork movement was expected. Thus, we attributed these events to dsDNA unwinding initiated from a nick and the appearance and subsequent growth of the dark regions along the DNA track represented ssDNA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the unidirectional nature of unwinding observed in the data.

claim: The unwinding rate of BLM from a nick is 60 ± 9 bp/s (mean ± SD) under 30 pN.
source: This yielded an unwinding rate of 60 ± 9 bp/s (mean ± SD) under 30 pN (Figure 1E and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative experimental data.

claim: BLM exclusively employed the intact ssDNA under tension as the track strand to unwind dsDNA.
source: The 4.2 kbp dsDNA segments in these 25 traces were always unwound while the 2.2 kbp dsDNA segments remained intact, independent of the orientation of the suspended nicked DNA (Figure 2B). These findings suggest that BLM exclusively employed the intact ssDNA under tension as the track strand to unwind dsDNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 25 out of 29 examined DNA molecules.

claim: The inability of BLM to unwind the 2.2 kbp dsDNA segment reinforced the conclusion that BLM alone unwinds unidirectionally from a nick.
source: In addition, the inability of BLM to unwind the 2.2 kbp dsDNA segment reinforced our conclusion that BLM alone unwinds unidirectionally from a nick.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observation that only one segment was unwound.

claim: RPA alone was incapable of unwinding dsDNA under external forces.
source: Control experiments confirmed that RPA alone was incapable of unwinding dsDNA under these external forces (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a control experiment confirming that RPA alone does not unwind DNA.

claim: In the presence of 200 nM BLM and RPA at various concentrations, DNA unwinding events initiated from the middle of the DNA template and the blunt-ended termini were observed.
source: In the presence of 200 nM BLM and RPA at various concentrations, DNA unwinding events initiated from the middle of the DNA template and the blunt-ended termini were observed (Figure 3A; Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in figures.

claim: With the increase of RPA concentration, the required force to monitor DNA unwinding significantly reduced.
source: With the increase of RPA concentration, the required force to monitor DNA unwinding indeed significantly reduced (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing force reduction with increasing RPA concentration.

claim: BLM/RPA-mediated DNA unwinding can take place in the absence of any externally applied force.
source: Moreover, we demonstrated that BLM/RPA-mediated DNA unwinding can even take place in the absence of any externally applied force (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the presence of 200 nM RPA and 20 nM BLM, half of examined traces exhibited continuous DNA unwinding at a low force of 5 pN.
source: It is noteworthy that with the presence of 200 nM RPA and 20 nM BLM, half of examined traces exhibited continuous DNA unwinding at a low force of 5 pN (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: On average, there were 3.4 independent unwinding events monitored on a single DNA molecule in the presence of 50 nM RPA and 200 nM BLM.
source: On average, there were 3.4 independent unwinding events monitored on a single DNA molecule, slightly higher than that without RPA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative experimental data.

claim: 53% of unwinding events (n = 40) showed bidirectional progression of dsDNA unwinding in the presence of 50 nM RPA and 200 nM BLM under 30 pN.
source: Strikingly, careful analyses of fluorescence images on the λ phage DNA under a force of 30 pN revealed that, in addition to the expected unidirectional unwinding events, 53% of them (n = 40) showed bidirectional progression of dsDNA unwinding (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 40 events.

claim: 26 out of 27 traces from experiments with the 6.4 kbp nicked DNA showed DNA unwinding in the presence of BLM and RPA.
source: In line with these observations, 26 out of 27 traces from the experiments with the 6.4 kbp nicked DNA showed DNA unwinding in the presence of BLM and RPA and 35% of them also exhibited BLM's bidirectional unwinding initiated from the single nick on the template (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 27 traces.

claim: 35% of unwinding events on the 6.4 kbp nicked DNA exhibited BLM's bidirectional unwinding initiated from the single nick.
source: In line with these observations, 26 out of 27 traces from the experiments with the 6.4 kbp nicked DNA showed DNA unwinding in the presence of BLM and RPA and 35% of them also exhibited BLM's bidirectional unwinding initiated from the single nick on the template (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: In most examined unwinding events (90%, n = 95), at least one bright spot locating at the end of the newly generated tensioned ssDNA was observed under 30 pN.
source: However, in most examined unwinding events (90%, n = 95), we observed at least one bright spot locating at the end of the newly generated tensioned ssDNA under 30 pN (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 95 events using eGFP-RPA.

claim: The bright spots observed with eGFP-RPA are attributed to unwound coiled ssDNA coated by RPA.
source: These spots increased in intensity as the unwinding fork progressed, and are thus attributed to unwound coiled ssDNA coated by RPA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that spots increase in intensity as unwinding progresses.

claim: 23 unwinding events were marked with two spots on both ends of an ssDNA, progressing in opposite directions.
source: Moreover, 23 unwinding events were marked with two spots on both ends of an ssDNA, progressing in opposite directions (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 23 events.

claim: The bidirectional unwinding only initiates from a nick instead of starting an opposite unwinding direction in the middle of an ongoing unidirectional unwinding.
source: Intriguingly, both Sytox and eGFP signals indicated that the bidirectional unwinding only initiates from a nick instead of starting an opposite unwinding direction in the middle of an ongoing unidirectional unwinding.
evidence: This is an inference based on fluorescence observations.

claim: The average bidirectional unwinding rate (117 ± 25 bp/s, mean ± SD) was 1.6-fold higher than that of the unidirectional unwinding (72 ± 24 bp/s, mean ± SD).
source: The average bidirectional unwinding rate (117 ± 25 bp/s, mean ± SD) was 1.6-fold higher than that of the unidirectional unwinding (72 ± 24 bp/s, mean ± SD) which is slightly faster than that with BLM alone (60 ± 9 bp/s, mean ± SD) (Figure 4C and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative experimental data.

claim: The unidirectional unwinding rate with RPA (72 ± 24 bp/s) is slightly faster than that with BLM alone (60 ± 9 bp/s).
source: The average bidirectional unwinding rate (117 ± 25 bp/s, mean ± SD) was 1.6-fold higher than that of the unidirectional unwinding (72 ± 24 bp/s, mean ± SD) which is slightly faster than that with BLM alone (60 ± 9 bp/s, mean ± SD) (Figure 4C and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative experimental data.

claim: Bidirectional DNA unwinding events were observable under low and zero external forces.
source: Notably, bidirectional DNA unwinding events were also observable under low and zero external forces (Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: hBLM alone initiates unidirectional unwinding from a nick.
source: When testing the homologous pair of hBLM and hRPA, results similar to the heterologous combination were obtained: hBLM alone initiates unidirectional unwinding from a nick and hRPA activates its bidirectional unwinding (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with human BLM.

claim: hRPA activates hBLM's bidirectional unwinding.
source: When testing the homologous pair of hBLM and hRPA, results similar to the heterologous combination were obtained: hBLM alone initiates unidirectional unwinding from a nick and hRPA activates its bidirectional unwinding (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with human BLM and RPA.

claim: Core-BLM alone unidirectionally unwinds dsDNA from a nick with a relatively slower rate compared with WT BLM.
source: Control experiments verified that core-BLM alone also unidirectionally unwinds dsDNA from a nick with a relatively slower rate compared with WT BLM (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing core-BLM to WT BLM.

claim: When RPA was present, both unidirectional (58%) and bidirectional (42%) unwinding events (n = 45) by core-BLM were recorded.
source: When RPA was present, both the unidirectional (58%) and bidirectional (42%) unwinding events (n = 45) by this mutant were recorded (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 45 events with core-BLM.

claim: The rate of bidirectional unwinding by core-BLM is 1.7-fold higher than that of unidirectional unwinding.
source: The rate of the bidirectional unwinding is 1.7-fold higher than that of the unidirectional unwinding, in agreement with the results with WT BLM (Figures 4C and 5D and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative experimental data.

claim: BLM's RPA-activated bidirectional unwinding possibly does not rely on the interactions between them.
source: These findings resemble the observations with WT BLM, reflecting that BLM's RPA-activated bidirectional unwinding possibly does not rely on the interactions between them.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that core-BLM lacking RPA-binding domains still shows bidirectional unwinding with RPA.

claim: In the buffer channel without BLM and RPA, the DNA length slowly decreased and the dark region along the DNA template gradually disappeared, indicating the reannealing of the unwound ssDNA (n = 30).
source: We found that, in the buffer channel, the DNA length slowly decreased and the dark region along the DNA template gradually disappeared, indicating the reannealing of the unwound ssDNA (n = 30, Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 30 traces.

claim: Up to 75% of traces (n = 53) in the RPA-only channel continued DNA unwinding.
source: In these experiments, we observed that up to 75% of traces (n = 53) in the following RPA channel continued DNA unwinding, and yet only 16% of traces showed continuous unwinding in the BLM channel (n = 38) (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 53 traces.

claim: Only 16% of traces showed continuous unwinding in the BLM-only channel (n = 38).
source: In these experiments, we observed that up to 75% of traces (n = 53) in the following RPA channel continued DNA unwinding, and yet only 16% of traces showed continuous unwinding in the BLM channel (n = 38) (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 38 traces.

claim: Free RPAs in solution are indispensable for promoting continuous dsDNA unwinding by BLM.
source: We thus conclude that free RPAs in solution are indispensable for promoting continuous dsDNA unwinding by BLM.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the channel-switching experiments showing that RPA is necessary for continued unwinding.

claim: Limited BLMs recognize and bind to nicks along the DNA template in the BLM channel, and they are stimulated by RPA to unwind a substantial distance without dissociation.
source: Since the BLM helicase has poor binding ability to intact dsDNA (Shi et al., 2017b), the immediate unwinding observed in the RPA channel suggest that limited BLMs recognize and bind to nicks along the DNA template in the BLM channel, and they are stimulated by RPA to unwind a substantial distance without dissociation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that unwinding continues immediately after switching to RPA channel.

claim: Only 17% of unwinding events (n = 33) showed continued unwinding when RPA-coated DNA template was transported to the BLM and RPA channel.
source: Only 17% of unwinding events (n = 33) showed continued unwinding in this channel (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), in disagreement with the recruitment model.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 33 events.

claim: Once BLM recognizes a nick and initiates unwinding with RPA, only free RPAs are indispensable for its processive unwinding.
source: In summary, we conclude that once BLM recognizes a nick and initiates unwinding with RPA, only free RPAs are indispensable for its processive unwinding.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the channel-switching experiments.

claim: ssDNA generated by BLM was immediately coated by free RPA, preventing the separated ssDNAs from reannealing.
source: These findings favor the model that ssDNA generated by BLM was immediately coated by free RPA, preventing the separated ssDNAs from reannealing.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: This is the first observation of helicase bidirectional unwinding from a nick.
source: This is the first observation, to our knowledge, of helicase bidirectional unwinding from a nick.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding.

claim: Previous studies of replicative and DNA repair helicases have reported bidirectional unwinding attributable to helicase melting dsDNA internally, which differs from the observed results.
source: Previous studies of replicative and DNA repair helicases have reported bidirectional unwinding attributable to helicase melting dsDNA internally, which differs from our observed results (Rad et al., 2015; Yardimci et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and contrasts with the current findings.

claim: The inability of BLM to unwind in the opposite direction is mostly likely due to the lack of tension on the relaxed ssDNA which might possibly promote the unwinding activity of BLM.
source: Since the physical barriers presented by dsDNA on both directions from a nick are similar, the inability of BLM to unwind in the opposite direction is mostly likely due to the lack of tension on the relaxed ssDNA which might possibly promote the unwinding activity of BLM.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed unidirectional unwinding.

claim: The core-BLM lacking the oligomerization domain exhibited unidirectional unwinding from a nick in the absence of RPA, leading to exclusion of the possibility that processive unwinding could depend on oligomerization of the protein.
source: The core-BLM lacking the oligomerization domain also exhibited unidirectional unwinding from a nick in the absence of RPA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1; Karow et al., 1999; Shi et al., 2017a), leading us to exclude the possibility that processive unwinding could depend on oligomerization of the protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data with core-BLM.

claim: Proteins at high concentrations might ensure sufficient binding of the enzyme to the ssDNA generated during an unwinding event, allowing for successive rounds of unwinding and preventing the unwound strands against reannealing.
source: Instead, proteins at high concentrations might ensure sufficient binding of the enzyme to the ssDNA generated during an unwinding event, allowing for successive rounds of unwinding and preventing the unwound strands against reannealing.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for why high protein concentrations are needed.

claim: The bidirectional unwinding necessitates the preloading of more than one helicase at the nick and subsequent binding of RPA on the newly generated ssDNA prolongs the binding and unwinding of BLM at the fork.
source: Thus, we reasoned that the bidirectional unwinding necessitates the preloading of more than one helicase at the nick and subsequent binding of RPA on the newly generated ssDNA prolongs the binding and unwinding of BLM at the fork.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: The unidirectional unwinding probably results from only one BLM helicase preloading at the nick and the inability of BLM to associate with RPA-coated ssDNA.
source: The unidirectional unwinding probably results from only one BLM helicase preloading at the nick and the inability of BLM to associate with RPA-coated ssDNA (Xue et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for unidirectional unwinding, supported by a citation.

claim: The long-range end resection in HR initiates from a nick generated by the MRN/X complex once the DSB ends are coated by DNA adducts.
source: Recent studies support a model that the long-range end resection in HR initiates from a nick generated by the MRN/X complex once the DSB ends are coated by DNA adducts (Cannavo and Cejka, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The abilities of BLM to recognize and preload on the nick would help identify the locations of DSB and possibly play a role in recruiting other required proteins for the resection.
source: It is highly likely that the abilities of BLM to recognize and preload on the nick would help identify the locations of DSB and possibly play a role in recruiting other required proteins for the resection.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the biological implications of the findings.

claim: The inherent ability of BLM and RPA to unwind bidirectionally from a nick would facilitate the resection by DNA adduct coated DSB ends.
source: Although it needs to be further validated, the inherent ability of BLM and RPA to unwind bidirectionally from a nick would facilitate the resection by DNA adduct coated DSB ends which provides ssDNA for the DNA2/EXO1 nucleases to degrade from 5' to 3' and the MRN complex to degrade from 3' to 5' (Symington, 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the biological implications, supported by a citation.

claim: Inhibition of MRN exonuclease activity only confers a relatively lower resection defect compared with the inhibition of its endonuclease activity.
source: Interestingly, inhibition of MRN exonuclease activity only confers a relatively lower resection defect compared with the inhibition of its endonuclease activity, suggesting that other proteins might also participate in the initial short ssDNA generation (Shibata et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.
